activities.caption: pair each link with its bookkeeping price
activities.name: thBondMatch

config.prompt: Pair each link with its strength:

pairs.right: 799 kJ/mol — part of why fuels burn

config.why: 679 broken, 862 formed — ΔH = −183 kJ/mol, close to the measured −185: the flame is the difference between average links held and better links made.

config.prompt: Burn 0.50 g of ethanol under 200 g of water; the water warms 20 °C, so q ≈ 16,700 J. What enthalpy per mole does the arithmetic give (ethanol: 46 g/mol)?
config.why: ≈1,540 kJ/mol against the textbook figure — the gap is real and instructive: heat escaped to the room, heated the can, vaporised fuel before combustion finished.
config.context: Insulation, flame shields and temperature extrapolation back to the moment of burning are the fixes — simple calorimetry always under-measures.

activities.anchor: The stored-energy picture survives in amended form
activities.caption: find the faulty line — what a bond actually stores
activities.name: thSnapSpot

config.prompt: A student retells the bond-energy story. One line is wrong — click it:
lines: Bonds are a low-energy state — which is why forming one pays energy back.
Pulling two partners apart costs energy.
If snapping apart paid out, everything around us would be drifting away while warming up.
Energy is stored in each link itself, waiting to be freed the moment it snaps.
The bookkeeping stands after one amendment: energy lives in the difference between weak and strong arrangements.
config.correction: Nothing waits inside a link to be freed — breaking COSTS energy; the ledger lives in the difference between weak and strong arrangements, which is what broken-minus-formed computes.
config.why: Low-energy state: snapping partners together releases; pulling them apart costs.

activities.caption: rebuild the unmeasurable enthalpy from measurable steps
activities.name: thHessOrder

config.prompt: Carbon to CO₂ directly resists measurement — rebuild the indirect path in order:
items: Add the steps like algebra — the enthalpies add
Sum: −394 kJ/mol, the true ΔH of combustion of carbon
config.why: Enthalpy is a state function: start and end decide, never the path — every formation-enthalpy table is this law industrialised.

activities.anchor: since T multiplies the entropy term
activities.caption: which family turns favourable only when hot?
activities.name: thDGTrace

config.prompt: ΔG plotted against temperature for three reaction families — which one becomes favourable only when hot?
config.why: Family B is endothermic but disorder-driven — dissolving, melting and boiling become favourable as heat magnifies the scatter; family A runs only cold; family C never stops.

activities.anchor: a local hot spot seeds the exothermic descent
activities.caption: true or false — why the fuel waits
activities.name: thSparkJudge

statements.s: Petrol's combustion is strongly exothermic, yet the tank sits safely beside air.
statements.why: Thermodynamically desperate, kinetically patient: nothing has climbed to the transition state.

statements.s: A spark works by supplying the whole ΔH of the reaction in advance.
statements.why: It ignites a patch over the barrier; the released heat then recruits the neighbours — the chain reaction of fire.

statements.s: Diamond turning into graphite is spontaneous — it simply takes geological timescales.
statements.why: Spontaneous does not mean fast — the kinetics chapter owns speed and the hill.

statements.s: A catalyst moves both endpoints of the energy profile so the reaction releases more.
statements.why: It offers a different route with a lower climb, holding reactants in a geometry that pre-pays part of it — and moves neither endpoint.
